'''Lee Lou-chuang''' ({{lang-zh|c=李羅權}}; born 20 April 1947), also known by his English name '''Louis Lee''', is a Taiwanese [[astrophysicist]], mathematician, and [[astronomer]].

== Early life and education ==
Lee was born in [[Tianwei, Changhua|Tianwei]], [[Changhua]], on April 20, 1947.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012 |title=Who's Who in the ROC [2012] |url=https://www.ey.gov.tw/upload/relfile/656/2561/6a40b688-46ef-48bb-a2a7-43aacb86b6d3.pdf |access-date=26 December 2025 |publisher=[[Executive Yuan]]}}</ref> After high school, he graduated from [[National Taiwan University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science]] (B.S.) in physics in 1969, then completed graduate studies in the United States at the [[California Institute of Technology]], where he earned his [[Master of Science]] (M.S.) in 1972 in physics and his [[Ph.D.]] in physics, mathematics, and [[astronomy]] in 1975. His doctoral dissertation was titled, "A Theory of Strong and Weak Scintillations with Applications to Astrophysics," and was completed under professors J. Randolph Jokipii, [[Jon Mathews]], and [[Gerald B. Whitham]] on a fellowship awarded by [[IBM]] and a grant by the [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite thesis |last=Lee |first=Lou-Chuang |title=A Theory of Strong and Weak Scintillations with Applications to Astrophysics |date=1975 |degree=PhD |publisher=California Institute of Technology |url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/9161/ |language=en}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
After receiving his doctorate, Lee worked at the [[Goddard Space Flight Center]] and taught at the [[University of Maryland]] before joining the [[University of Alaska]] faculty.

Lee returned to Taiwan and began teaching at [[National Cheng Kung University]] in 1995.<ref>{{cite news|title=Professor Lou-Chuang Lee|url=http://aappsdpp.org/AAPPSDPPF/DPPIHAC/L%20C%20Lee.pdf|accessdate=4 July 2016}}</ref> He has served as the director of the [[National Applied Research Laboratories]] and the [[National Space Organization|National Space Program Office]] (NSPO).<ref>{{cite news|last1=Chiu|first1=Yu-Tzu|title=Regional disaster relief center opens in Taipei|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2005/12/27/2003286204|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=27 December 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Chiu|first1=Yu-Tzu|title=ROCSAT-2 gets off the ground|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2004/05/22/2003156480|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=22 May 2004}}</ref> As leader of the NSPO, Lee presided over the launch of the satellite [[ROCSAT-2]] and the development of [[Constellation Observing System for Meteorology, Ionosphere, and Climate|ROCSAT-3]].<ref>{{cite news|last1=Chiu|first1=Yu-Tzu|title=Satellite will yield more than images|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2004/05/24/2003156733|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=24 May 2005}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Chiu|first1=Yu-Tzu|title=US 'eye in the sky' to help observe Taiwan's weather|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/local/archives/2001/05/04/0000084308|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=4 May 2001}}</ref> Lee also helped conduct research on thunderclouds and the ionosphere.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Chiu|first1=Yu-tzu|title=Taiwanese research makes waves|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2003/06/27/2003056893|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=27 June 2003}}</ref>

Lee later became president of [[National Central University]] and was named minister of the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (Taiwan)|National Science Council]] in April 2008.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hirsch|first1=Max|title=Local star-gazer discovers comet|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2007/07/28/2003371574|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=28 July 2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Wang|first1=Flora|title=Liu names major Cabinet posts|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2008/04/29/2003410546/2|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=29 April 2008}}</ref> Lee was replaced by [[Cyrus Chu]] in February 2011.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Shih|first1=Hsiu-chuan|title=Wu reshuffles some Cabinet posts|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/front/archives/2011/02/02/2003495017|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=2 February 2011}}</ref>

==Honors==
Lee was elected a member of [[Academia Sinica]] in 2002,<ref>{{cite news |title=Lou-Chuang Lee |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=231 |access-date=10 September 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref><ref name="appt">{{cite news|last1=Lu|first1=Meggie|title=Premier-designate Liu names second wave of Cabinet member appointees|url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2008/04/29/2003410557|accessdate=4 July 2016|work=Taipei Times|date=29 April 2008}}</ref> and a foreign member of the [[United States National Academy of Engineering]] in 2018.<ref>{{cite news |title=Professor Lou-Chang Lee |url=https://www.nae.edu/178240/Professor-LouChuang-Lee |access-date=10 September 2023 |publisher=United States National Academy of Engineering}}</ref>
